solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: This is Q1, isn't it?

parts.note: Q1 is the first question in a list, so it leads the others; and a question ending in isn't it? steers the listener towards the answer yes

explanation.surface: Someone points at the first question on a quiz sheet and asks for confirmation.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses meet: the question that comes first, and a question phrased to push for a particular reply, as a tag like 'isn't it?' does.
explanation.definitionFit: A question worded to prompt the reply the asker wants is the courtroom and journalism term for this kind of query.

clue.text: Support friend in law

parts.note: a leg is what supports a table or chair
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone backs a companion who has married into the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'friend in law' reads like 'friend-in-law', a relative by marriage, but 'in law' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something lawfully, within what statutes permit, is acting in accordance with the law.

clue.text: A professional name for part of a stage

parts.note: pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: An actor's agent describes a well-known performer's place in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatres the forward section of stage projecting in front of the curtain carries this name.

clue.text: Burning, losing a couple of thousand due to rising prices

indicators.note: losing tells us letters are dropped from the word for burning

parts.note: inflammation is a burning soreness in the body
taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them give MM

explanation.surface: An economic commentary blames soaring costs on a heated market cooling by a few thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes AMM from the middle of INFLAMMATION, leaving INFLATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Economists use this term for a general, sustained increase in the cost of goods.

clue.text: People invited invest time in speculation

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for time sits inside the word for speculation

parts.note: a guess is a speculation

explanation.surface: Those on the invitation list put their time into risky financial ventures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invest' is a link word here, meaning put; T goes inside GUESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Those asked to a party or a house as visitors are guests by invitation.

clue.text: Some speed reduction can be part of fighter's armoury

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine, and an upper is a dose of such a stimulant
a cut is a reduction

explanation.surface: Slowing down a bit is presented as a tactic a combatant might use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speed' looks like velocity, but it is the drug; an UPPER is a stimulant pill.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's rising punch to the chin is one of the blows in a pugilist's repertoire.

clue.text: Manifestation of good in evil?

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for good is placed inside the word for evil

parts.note: sin is evil-doing, wickedness

explanation.surface: A moral question: is there a trace of goodness in wickedness?
explanation.definitionFit: An indication or visible evidence of something is a sign of it.

clue.text: Not moving prisoner outside a part of the UK

indicators.note: outside tells us the word for prisoner wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: an inmate is someone held in a prison
NI stands for Northern Ireland, one of the four parts of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A convict stands motionless outside one of the British home nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' has the prisoner word wrap around the rest; NI for Northern Ireland is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lifeless or motionless is described as without life or movement.

clue.text: Racing certainty with no airs

definitions.meaning: someone or something sure to succeed, a certainty
unaffected and unpretentious, without putting on airs

explanation.definitionFit: A natural is a sure winner, and the adjective describes someone free of affectation.

clue.text: Animal's mistake, crossing one river

indicators.note: crossing tells us the word for mistake spans across the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder or mistake
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An animal blunders while wading across a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Animal' stands for 'is'. I and R go inside GAFFE, after its G.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-necked African mammal is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Show maturity, collared by quiet worker

indicators.note: collared by means grabbed round the neck, so the word for maturity is enclosed by the other pieces

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
the ant is the crossword's classic worker insect
age can mean maturity, as in coming of age

explanation.surface: A display of grown-up behaviour is caught by a silent labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collared by' pictures one piece held round the neck by the others; P for quiet comes from musical notation.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacular procession or public display is a type of show.

clue.text: Dilapidated ancestral house

indicators.note: a dilapidated building is falling to pieces, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A family seat is falling into ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' looks like a building, but it is a royal dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal dynasty of Henry IV, V and VI was a branch of the Plantagenets, an English royal house.

clue.text: Good Queen Bess's mole

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good in crosswords
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth, known as Good Queen Bess

explanation.surface: A spy is uncovered in the court of Elizabeth I.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' suggests a spy or a burrowing animal; here it is a breakwater.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a massive stone breakwater or jetty, much like a landing stage projecting into the sea.

clue.text: Professional American's positive response with 12 unfinished

parts.note: yup is an American informal yes

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is lopped off the answer to clue 12

parts.note: the answer to 12 across is a jetty

explanation.surface: A career-minded person from the States agrees, with a reference to another clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1980s label for a young urban professional is used as a noun for such a person.

clue.text: Something to write on page merchant prepared

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, worked into shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trader readies a sheet for writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Treated animal skin was the traditional writing material before paper.

clue.text: Go bottom and leg it

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in it is your go
the tail is the bottom or rear end

explanation.surface: An instruction to head for the bottom and run.
explanation.definitionFit: Running away in fright, fleeing, is to show one's back to the enemy.

clue.text: Live close by developing region with hub

indicators.note: developing means changing and growing, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A district growing up around a central point is pleasantly close.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to border or adjoin something is to be situated next to it.

clue.text: Insect that's found in objects of limited value

definitions.meaning: The genus of the mayfly, a short-lived insect
things of only passing interest or use, such as old tickets and leaflets

explanation.definitionFit: The mayfly genus takes its name from short life, and short-lived collectables share the same word.

clue.text: Standard bargains which you find at the greengrocer's?

definitions.text: which you find at the greengrocer's?

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
snips are bargains, things cheap at the price

explanation.surface: Ordinary cheap deals, the sort a vegetable shop might offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Root vegetables sold by the fruit and veg seller are examples of what is found there.

clue.text: Carriage or stanhope redesigned without top

indicators.note: redesigned means the remaining letters are arranged in a new form
without top means the first letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: A light horse-drawn vehicle is rebuilt minus its hood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without top' takes S off STANHOPE, and 'redesigned' turns TANHOPE into the answer. A stanhope is itself a light carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A light open four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle is a type of carriage.

clue.text: Bird or other creature that might fly — with time!

parts.note: from the saying pigs might fly, about something unlikely
an eon is a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: A bird, or the farmyard animal of the saying, might take to the air given long enough.
explanation.definitionFit: The common town dove is an example of a bird.

clue.text: At the moment, present is not to be found

parts.note: now means at the present moment
here means present, as when answering a register

explanation.surface: Right now, a gift has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' tempts as a gift; it means in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in no place at all is a way of saying it cannot be located.

clue.text: Ties up in beds?

definitions.meaning: to moor a ship at a quay
sleeping places on a ship or train

explanation.definitionFit: A ship moors at a quay, and bunks on board or in a sleeper train share this name.

clue.text: Pain caused by trapping horse's head in crack

indicators.note: trapping means holding inside, so the word for crack encloses the pick

parts.note: crack as an adjective means first-rate, an ace

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Discomfort from a horse catching its head in a fissure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like a split; it means expert, ACE, which holds H.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull persistent hurt is a synonym of pain.

clue.text: The cause of a dark look?

definitions.text: The cause of a dark look?

parts.words: The cause of a dark look?
parts.note: a dark look usually means a scowl, but here it is literal: cosmetics that darken the lids

explanation.surface: A question about what makes someone glare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dark look' suggests a glare, but it is literal: make-up that darkens the area round the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic colour applied to the eyelids gives the eyes a shaded, darker appearance.

clue.text: Knight on road from city abroad

parts.note: to dub is to make someone a knight with a tap of the sword
the A1 is Britain's Great North Road, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A knight sets off on a road from a foreign city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulf emirate's capital is a city outside the UK.

clue.text: Area of London with no drunk

parts.note: W1 is London's West End postcode district, written WI in crosswords
taken as written

explanation.surface: A part of the capital with no drinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual drinker of cheap wine is an alcoholic, a noun sense of drunk.

clue.text: Most of those people enjoy similar things

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: they refers to those people
to like something is to enjoy it

explanation.surface: Most of them enjoy comparable things.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'and the like' means and other things of a comparable kind.

clue.text: The Yorkshire currency is a load of bother

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect the is clipped to t'
the rouble is the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: A Yorkshireman complains that money is all hassle.
explanation.walkthrough: In Yorkshire speech 'the' is shortened to t', as in 'on t' moor'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bother means difficulty or fuss, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Moving on can revitalise conscription

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting going can give someone a new lease of life, as compulsory army duty might.
explanation.definitionFit: Compulsory peacetime military duty in Britain, ended in 1960, is a form of conscription.
